miniProject.title: Train, resume and sample the tiny decoder
miniProject.brief: Turn the decoder into a trained model you can trust: a loss you can derive by hand, a loop that resumes exactly, and decoding policies whose distributions you can check. Train on the packed split from section 1 on a CPU or a free GPU notebook.
steps: Implement cross-entropy, gradient clipping, AdamW, the warmup-cosine schedule, get_batch and checkpointing, and pass the CS336 tests in test_nn_utils.py, test_optimizer.py, test_data.py and test_serialization.py.
Run two controls before any real run: drive one tiny batch to near-zero loss, and confirm that a run on shuffled targets leaves validation loss near the unigram baseline.
Train on your section 1 split with a fixed seed, logging loss, gradient norm, learning rate and tokens seen, with a validation curve from the held-out split.
Save complete state, including model, optimizer, step, RNG and data cursor, and show that an interrupted run matches an uninterrupted one to a stated level.
Implement greedy, temperature, top-k and top-p sampling with EOS and length stops, and reproduce fixed-seed outputs exactly.
Connect the atlas lab adapters for section 3 and pass tests/test_s3_training.py.
deliverables: The training script and config, with the checkpoint format documented.
The training log and validation curve for your run, plus the two control runs.
A resume-equivalence result: the steps compared, the tolerance and why it is the right one.
Sample outputs for each decoding policy from one prompt and seed, with the config that reproduces them.

checks.name: CS336 tests for cross-entropy, clipping, AdamW, the schedule, data loading and checkpointing
checks.command: uv run pytest tests/test_nn_utils.py tests/test_optimizer.py tests/test_data.py tests/test_serialization.py

checks.name: Atlas lab, section 3: loss threshold, resume equivalence and sampling filters
checks.note: Run in labs/llm-foundations of an ai-atlas clone after you connect adapters.py to your package. The threshold test trains on a Markov chain with a known entropy rate: validation loss must approach that rate, and a loss below it means the labels leak. Resume must match an uninterrupted run exactly on CPU.

rubric.pass: Your cross-entropy passes the public test, including the overflow case.
rubric.strong: You derive one masked loss by hand and match your code, and the shuffled-target control behaves as you predicted.

rubric.pass: Validation loss falls on your split and the section 3 lab threshold test passes.
rubric.strong: The log shows learning rate, gradient norm and tokens seen, and you explain one anomaly from it.

rubric.pass: An interrupted run continues without a loss jump.
rubric.strong: Losses after resume match the uninterrupted run exactly on CPU, and your stated GPU tolerance is justified.

rubric.pass: Each policy runs and stops on EOS or the length cap.
rubric.strong: Fixed-seed outputs reproduce exactly, and you show by hand how temperature followed by top-p changes the kept set at one step.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone artifact 2: the trained checkpoint and its decoding policies. Section 4 evaluates this checkpoint, and section 5 must reproduce its greedy outputs with a cache.
